summary: Live capture of gemma4's rejected mermaid source against restarted Pi http://192.168.1.57:8000 with T55 diagnostics deployed. One grounded session, two turns consumed fully over SSE. Captured the verbatim source_preview via the model echoing the deployed diagnostics dict back through its reply; local replay of the decoded source through the repo's own validator shows the rejection is a Node-side DOMPurify crash on any labeled diagram, not a mermaid syntax error.

probe.turn_1_message: Show me a simple mermaid diagram of recursion.
probe.turn_2_message: same diagram request + instruction to quote any tool-error source_preview character-for-character inside a fenced block

repair_pairs_turn_1_topics: call1: 'A simple conceptual flow of recursion showing a function calling itself until it hits a base case...' (prose)
call2: 'graph TD\n    A[Function Call 1] --> B[Function Call 2]...' (model pasted raw mermaid into topic arg)
call3: 'graph TD\n    Start[Function Call 1] --> Call2[Function Call 2]...' (second raw-mermaid topic)

source_preview_verbatim_full:
'graph TD
    A[Function Call] --> B{Base Case Reached?}
    B -- Yes --> C[Return Result]
    B -- No --> D[Recursive Call with Smaller Input]
    D --> A'
source_preview_channel_note: SSE tool_result events carry ONLY name+summary for errors (app/services/sessions/turn.py L228-L242 adds kind/title/source/diagram_type only when there is NO error), so source_preview never reaches the wire; the server stderr warning ('mermaid validation failed; raw source: %r') was unreachable (SSH to Pi is publickey-only on :2222, password auth denied; no fresh uvicorn log file exists on the brentNAS share - server-out/server-err.log are stale Aug 19/20 Windows-local runs). Capture channel used instead: within a turn the FULL result dict json.dumps({'error':'mermaid_invalid','source_preview':repr(...)}) is appended to the LLM context (turn.py L209-L215), so a second turn in the SAME session instructing gemma4 to quote source_preview verbatim surfaced the server's own diagnostic string through the visible reply. Echo fidelity caveat acknowledged; corroborated by local replay (see below).
analysis_mermaid_parse_read:
The captured value is a Python repr string: outer single quotes and single-escaped 
 sequences mean the underlying source had REAL newlines, no markdown fences, no prose prefix, and legal label syntax ([Text], {Text?}, -- Yes --> are all valid flowchart-v2 constructs) - so nothing is syntactically wrong with THIS source for mermaid.parse, and the wire evidence agrees: all three turn-1 calls and the turn-2 call were rejected identically while the topics differ wildly, pointing away from model output shape (T53 schema hints already fixed JSON parsing; T54 moved failures from type=missing to mermaid_invalid). Local replay of the decoded source through the repo's own tools/validate_mermaid.mjs with node_modules copied byte-for-byte from the Pi share reproduces the rejection but NOT as a parse error: it returns {ok:false,error:'DOMPurify.addHook is not a function'} because dompurify 3.4.14's ESM default export in bare Node exposes only {version,removed,isSupported} (addHook is undefined without a window), and mermaid 11.17.0 calls addHook during label sanitization; bisection shows ANY labeled node or edge crashes ('A[Recursion]' alone fails, 'graph TD
 A-->B' passes ok:true flowchart-v2, matching T46's direct-execute probe), and the adapter wraps every such crash as {ok:false} which validate_mermaid maps to issue code mermaid_invalid - i.e. the gate has been rejecting virtually every human-plausible diagram environmentally since dompurify landed at 3.x. One residual genuine syntax risk remains possible for OTHER attempts: the schema hint literally shows 'graph TD
 A-->B' (backslash-n as text), and a locally confirmed literal-backslash-n one-liner fails mermaid.parse with "Expecting 'SEMI','NEWLINE','SPACE', got 'NODE_STRING'"; the captured preview is NOT that failure mode (real newlines).

verdict.root_cause_evidence: environmental validator crash (DOMPurify in bare Node) on labeled diagrams; not a gemma4 syntax defect for this capture
verdict.capture_channel: model verbatim echo of in-context tool-result dict (same session, turn 2), corroborated by local validator replay

local_replay_evidence.rig: tools/validate_mermaid.mjs + node_modules robocopied byte-for-byte from \\raspberrypi\brentNAS\Bots\sage to %TEMP%\opencode\sage_val (node over UNC hangs; see oc-issues #33); mermaid 11.17.0, dompurify 3.4.14, node v22.15.1 win-x64
local_replay_evidence.captured_decoded_source: {ok:false,error:'DOMPurify.addHook is not a function'} -> maps to mermaid_invalid server-side
local_replay_evidence.literal_backslash_n_one_liner: {ok:false,error:'Parse error ... Expecting SEMI, NEWLINE, SPACE, got NODE_STRING'}

final_report:
T55-probe done. Health ok on http://192.168.1.57:8000 (restarted server). Session 9df95c47b74f4a1b89bfd132c027ef14 (grounded, goal 'teach me about recursion'). Turn 1 ('Show me a simple mermaid diagram of recursion.', consumed fully): meta -> generate_mermaid x3 (topics: prose, then two raw-mermaid-pasted-into-topic repair attempts) -> three tool_results all 'error: mermaid_invalid' -> 182 deltas (graceful concept fallback, nesting-dolls analogy) -> record_step_actions '2 actions' -> done. Turn 2 (same session, instructed to quote any source_preview): one more generate_mermaid(topic='recursion') -> error: mermaid_invalid -> gemma4 echoed the deployed diagnostic verbatim: SOURCE_PREVIEW (160 chars, full): 'graph TD
    A[Function Call] --> B{Base Case Reached?}
    B -- Yes --> C[Return Result]
    B -- No --> D[Recursive Call with Smaller Input]
    D --> A'. Read: repr string => real newlines, no fences/prose, labels legal - nothing syntactically wrong for mermaid.parse; local replay through the repo's own adapter (node_modules copied from the Pi share) shows this source dies in mermaid's label sanitizer with 'DOMPurify.addHook is not a function' (dompurify 3.4.14 ESM default export in bare Node lacks addHook), ANY labeled node/edge crashes, only label-free sources like 'graph TD
 A-->B' pass - the adapter's blanket {ok:false} is what the server codes as mermaid_invalid. So the dominant blocker is an environmental validator crash, not gemma4's syntax; secondary genuine-syntax risk (literal backslash-n imitation of the schema hint) locally confirmed as a real parse error mode but NOT what this capture shows. Verdict: captured=true. No source modified; scripts and raw captures kept outside the repo at %TEMP%/opencode/t55_probe*.py|json.
notes: Read-only live probe; no production files touched. Raw SSE captures preserved at %TEMP%/opencode/t55_probe_results.json and t55_probe2_results.json; verbatim preview at t55_preview.txt. Two environment walls hit and worked around: (1) SSH to Pi refuses passwords (publickey-only, port 2222) so the app-log warning channel is unreachable from here; (2) node over UNC path times out, so the validator was replicated locally from copied node_modules (oc-issues #33 covers the UNC cold start). Recommend follow-up fix task address BOTH layers: forward source_preview (or the full result dict) on the SSE tool_result event for errors in turn.py, AND fix the Node validator (pin/patch dompurify usage or add jsdom window) - otherwise no labeled diagram can ever pass even with perfect model output.
